skill.name: ghe-status
skill.description: Read-only GitHub Elements status overview for active threads, phase distribution, available work, and workflow health indicators.
skill.summary: Shows a quick read-only status overview for GitHub Elements workflows.
skill.author: Emasoft

security_audit.summary: Most external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code and fenced output examples. The hidden home directory access is confirmed because a read-only status skill grants write scope to ~/.claude. Semantic review also found absolute behavioral override language and mandatory report posting that conflict with read-only expectations.

remediation.issue: Hidden home configuration access in a read-only status skill.
remediation.suggestion: Remove ~/.claude from the allowed write locations, or require explicit user confirmation in a separate maintenance skill.

remediation.issue: Absolute instruction hierarchy inside the skill text.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the IRON LAW section with neutral guidance that respects platform, developer, safety, and user instructions.

remediation.issue: Status workflow mandates posting full reports to GitHub issue threads.
remediation.suggestion: Make external posting opt-in and keep the default status response local and read-only.

remediation.issue: Read-only description conflicts with write boundary instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Move background-agent write boundaries into the skills that actually modify issues, reports, or settings.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 44 is a Markdown naming template inside inline code formatting, not Ruby or shell execution. No command is invoked or constructed.
Line 45 documents a timestamp format using inline code formatting. It contains no executable command or user-controlled command string.
Line 57 names a local settings file in Markdown formatting. The text describes settings awareness and does not execute a command.
Line 58 documents the enabled setting using Markdown inline code. There is no shell, Ruby, or dynamic execution behavior.
Line 59 documents the notification_level setting using Markdown inline code. It is descriptive text, not executable code.
Line 88 starts a fenced Markdown output example. The fenced block shows report formatting and does not contain commands to run.
Line 104 closes the fenced Markdown example. This is formatting syntax and not external command execution.
Line 31 explicitly allows writes to ~/.claude for plugin or settings fixes. A read-only status skill should not authorize modification of hidden home configuration.
The skill grants access to a hidden home directory that can affect Claude configuration. This is a real filesystem risk even without a concrete write command.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: The skill states "THIS LAW IS ABSOLUTE" and tells the agent to follow every user word verbatim with no exceptions. This can conflict with higher-priority safety and workflow instructions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The language is directive, absolute, and attempts to control agent behavior across tasks. It does not explicitly say to ignore system instructions, so confidence is high but not maximal.

semantic_findings.title: Read-Only Claim Conflicts With Write Permissions
semantic_findings.description: The skill says its purpose is read-only, but it also defines writable background-agent locations including the project, parent directory, ~/.claude, and /tmp. This mismatch can cause unexpected file changes during a status workflow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The write boundary text and read-only purpose are both present in the same file. The skill does not include direct write commands, so the risk is contextual rather than immediate execution.

semantic_findings.title: Mandatory External Report Posting
semantic_findings.description: The skill mandates posting full reports to a GitHub issue thread and to GHE_REPORTS. This creates an external publication side effect that does not match a simple status check.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly requires full report text to be posted to a GitHub issue thread. It is prose rather than executable code, but the intended side effect is clear.

content.value_statement: Teams need a quick view of GitHub Elements workflow health without changing issue state. This skill produces a read-only status overview for active threads, phases, and warnings.
actual_capabilities: Requests a GitHub Elements status report through the reporter agent.
Summarizes active DEV, TEST, and REVIEW threads.
Shows phase distribution across active workflow items.
Lists available work that is ready but not claimed.
Highlights workflow health indicators, violations, and checkpoint frequency.
Respects local settings that can disable or reduce status output.
limitations: It is intended for status review, not issue claiming or phase transitions.
It depends on GitHub Elements labels and reporter-agent behavior.
It does not provide detailed metrics or epic-specific reports.
Local settings can reduce the amount of information returned.

use_cases.title: Start a Coordination Session
use_cases.description: Get a quick overview of active work before assigning or reviewing GitHub Elements issues.

use_cases.title: Check Review Load
use_cases.description: See how many items are in DEV, TEST, and REVIEW before planning the next handoff.

use_cases.title: Find Ready Work
use_cases.description: Identify ready issues that are not claimed without changing the workflow state.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Status Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a current overview.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the current GitHub Elements status overview.

prompt_templates.title: Phase Summary
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request focused on workflow distribution.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show active GitHub Elements threads and summarize the DEV, TEST, and REVIEW phase counts.

prompt_templates.title: Available Work Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request before selecting the next issue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check GitHub Elements status and highlight ready work that is not claimed.

prompt_templates.title: Health-Focused Status Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for coordination risk review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a GitHub Elements status overview with active threads, phase distribution, recent completions, and workflow health warnings.

output_examples.input: Show the current GitHub Elements status.
output_examples.output: The response summarizes active threads, phase counts, available work, and workflow health indicators in a compact status report.

output_examples.input: What work is ready but not claimed?
output_examples.output: The response lists ready issues that are not assigned, with enough context to choose the next action.

output_examples.input: Give me a health check for the workflow.
output_examples.output: The response calls out violations, checkpoint frequency, and recent completions so the team can spot coordination issues.

best_practices: Use this skill at session start before claiming or transitioning issues.
Keep local settings current so disabled or reduced output is intentional.
Use ghe-report when you need detailed metrics or epic-specific analysis.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to claim issues or change issue phases.
Do not treat the status overview as a full audit or detailed report.
Do not post status information externally unless the user explicitly requests it.

faq.question: Does this skill change GitHub issues?
faq.answer: No. It is intended for read-only status checks and overview reporting.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I use ghe-report instead?
faq.answer: Use ghe-report for detailed metrics, health checks, or epic-specific reports.

faq.question: Can it show active workflow phases?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to show active DEV, TEST, and REVIEW threads.

faq.question: Does it respect local settings?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill describes settings that can disable or reduce output verbosity.

faq.question: Is this a security or compliance audit tool?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow status and health indicators, not a full security audit.
